description: Feature backlog - Product Owner owns priority

items.title: backlog check should show which verify command failed
items.intent: When backlog check <ID> fails an AC verify command, the output must print the exact command that failed and its exit code so a developer can reproduce and debug the failure without guessing which check broke.
steps: In cmd-backlog-read.sh, in the AC verify loop, capture the exit code of each verify command
When a verify command fails (exit code != 0), print the command text and exit code before the failure message
Keep format consistent with existing log_* style

acceptanceCriteria.text: Failed verify command text appears in backlog check output
acceptanceCriteria.verify: tid=$(.aishore/aishore backlog add --json "{\"title\":\"_groom_ac_test\",\"intent\":\"groom test intent placeholder twenty chars\",\"type\":\"feat\",\"priority\":\"could\",\"steps\":[\"implement the test feature\"],\"acceptanceCriteria\":[{\"text\":\"fails\",\"verify\":\"exit 99\"}],\"readyForSprint\":false}" 2>&1 | grep -oE "[A-Z]+-[0-9]+"); out=$(.aishore/aishore backlog check "$tid" 2>&1); .aishore/aishore backlog rm "$tid" --force 2>/dev/null; echo "$out" | grep -q "exit 99"

items.groomingNotes: AC creates a temp item with a known-failing verify command, runs check, confirms the command text appears in output, then cleans up. Fully behavioral and self-contained.
